question.text: Under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act 1967, the Central Government has the power to do which of the following?

answer.text: Freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets/economic resources of individuals or entities listed in the Schedule to the Order, or of persons engaged in or suspected of terrorism
Only issue warnings to individuals suspected of terrorism
Grant amnesty to entities voluntarily disclosing terror financing
Delegate all enforcement powers to state governments

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes Section 51A of UAPA as conferring three Central Government powers: (1) freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets/economic resources of listed individuals or entities or of persons engaged in or suspected of terrorism, (2) prohibit anyone from making funds, financial assets, or related services available to such listed persons, and (3) prevent entry into or transit through India of such listed individuals. The Trap: The other options shrink Section 51A to mere warnings, invent an amnesty mechanism, or wrongly delegate enforcement to state governments — none of which appears in the workbook. Note: The three powers under Section 51A are limited to the freeze/seize/attach, prohibit-availability, and entry-prevention measures as listed in the workbook.
